concerns.description: Envelope approval, revision identity, sequence correlation, mode ownership and decision provenance
concerns.rationale: Typed contracts and one logical producer express discrete responsibility without prescribing the control implementation.

concerns.description: Periodic release and reaction deadline change acceptable system behavior
concerns.rationale: Activation admits a reaction but does not constrain clock, release jitter, sample age or completion time.

concerns.description: Explicit inhibited/startup behavior and nonautomatic recovery
concerns.rationale: Modes can be domain data; hazard-specific transition and recovery obligations need contracts beyond a graph.

concerns.description: A deterministic synchronous controller implementation realizes ReactToFlightTick; an RTOS adapter releases ticks and latches outputs. The graph does not supply synchronous semantics.
concerns.rationale: A thread, synchronous node or PLC task is a realization of the same responsibility; the mechanism alone does not discharge requirements.

concerns.description: AADL analysis maps the controller, sensor buses and actuator driver to processors and connections; replicas implement one logical owner. Core affinity and network scheduling are L2 until an explicit independence requirement makes them contractual.
concerns.rationale: Physical mapping and latency budgets need deployment-specific evidence, separate from logical ownership.

concerns.description: Sensor-fusion equations, stability margins, actuator dynamics, synchronous control-law causality and voting failure assumptions
concerns.rationale: A matching typed interface cannot define the external tool model of computation, prove safety, or solve physical equations.

facets.meaning: Illustrative release-to-command requirement measured on one monotonic clock; period changes require domain review.
obligations: Offline inequality validation is not a WCET proof, schedulability analysis, timer implementation or runtime safety proof.
Specify release jitter, clock error, sample-age bound, execution platform and interrupt/bus interference before analysis.
Deadline is measured from scheduled release to command acceptance at the I/O boundary, not merely process return; include communication delay.
Missed releases and expired outputs require independently assessed monitoring; do not queue unbounded catch-up reactions.

facets.meaning: Modes and reset semantics remain domain vocabulary; this sidecar proposes obligations, not executable transition logic.
obligations: Define transition priority and handling of simultaneous reset/fault inputs in the specialized model.
Assess safe outputs and monitor independence against domain hazards; neither naming a mode nor parsing this file proves safety.

realization.strategy: A deterministic synchronous controller implementation realizes ReactToFlightTick; an RTOS adapter releases ticks and latches outputs. The graph does not supply synchronous semantics.
realization.placement: AADL analysis maps the controller, sensor buses and actuator driver to processors and connections; replicas implement one logical owner. Core affinity and network scheduling are L2 until an explicit independence requirement makes them contractual.
limitations: No executable control law, hardware binding or analyzer result is included.
Single logical owner does not provide physical redundancy, mutual exclusion or exactly-once actuation.
Policy and clinical/operator authorization are implementation prerequisites, not asserted by these policy-free interface sketches.

artifacts.claim: Interface and explanatory pseudocode only; no control analyzer, code generator or hardware test executed.
Analysis inputs and mapping questions only; not an executable AADL model or schedulability result.
